retriever_type.description: Retriever protocol class. Determines transport (IMAP/POP3), encryption (SSL/plain), and delivery mode (simple/multidrop). Common values: SimpleIMAPSSLRetriever, SimplePOP3SSLRetriever, SimpleIMAPRetriever, SimplePOP3Retriever

retriever_server.description: Hostname or IP address of the incoming mail server

retriever_port.description: TCP port of the mail server. Standard ports: 993 (IMAPS), 143 (IMAP STARTTLS), 995 (POP3S), 110 (POP3)

retriever_username.description: Login name for the mail account, typically the full e-mail address

retriever_password.description: Plaintext password for the mail account. Ignored when retriever_password_command is set

retriever_password_command.description: Shell command as an argument list whose stdout is read as the password (e.g. a pass/secret-tool call). Set to null to use retriever_password instead

items.description: One argv element of the password command (e.g. '/usr/bin/pass' or 'email/work')

retriever_mailboxes.description: IMAP mailboxes to retrieve messages from. Only relevant for IMAP retriever types; ignored for POP3

items.description: IMAP mailbox name exactly as it appears on the server (e.g. INBOX, Sent, Drafts)

destination_type.description: Delivery method. Maildir is recommended for reliability. Options: Maildir, Mboxrd, MDA_external, MDA_qmaillocal

destination_path.description: Filesystem path to the Maildir directory or mbox file; or path to the MDA executable when destination_type is MDA_external

destination_arguments.description: Argument list passed to the MDA executable. Only used when destination_type is MDA_external; set to null otherwise

items.description: One argument token passed to the MDA program

filters.description: Message filters applied to each message before delivery. Each entry produces a [filter] section. Typical use: spam tagging (SpamAssassin), DKIM checking

type.description: Filter class name (Filter_external runs an arbitrary program; Filter_classifier is for trainable classifiers)

path.description: Absolute path to the filter program executable

arguments.description: Arguments passed to the filter executable; set to null to omit the arguments line

options_read_all.description: If true, retrieve all messages present on the server. If false, skip messages whose UID was already retrieved in a previous session

options_delete.description: If true, delete messages from the server immediately after successful local delivery. Use with caution — set to false until delivery is verified

options_message_log.description: Absolute or tilde-expanded path to the retrieval log file. Set to an empty string to disable logging entirely

options_verbose.description: Log verbosity: 0=silent (errors only), 1=normal one-line status per session, 2=verbose per-message output for debugging

options_received.description: If true, prepend a Received: header to each message documenting when and from where it was retrieved

options_delivered_to.description: If true, prepend a Delivered-To: header containing the envelope recipient address

options_max_message_size.description: Skip retrieval of any message larger than this many bytes. Set to 0 to retrieve messages of any size

options_max_bytes_per_session.description: Stop the retrieval session after downloading this many bytes. Useful to cap bandwidth per run. Set to 0 for no limit

options_delete_after.description: Delete messages from the server that are older than this many days, regardless of whether they have been retrieved. Set to 0 to disable

options_delete_bigger_than.description: Delete messages larger than this many bytes from the server without downloading them. Set to 0 to disable
